requirement:
Build a scalable URL shortener from scratch. Analyze this requirement using
docs/01-business-requirement.md, docs/02-requirement-analysis.md, and
docs/03-engineering-design.md.

Preserve the design's stack: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy 2.x,
PostgreSQL, and Redis. Include an API to create a short link, a redirect for
known codes, and click analytics. Preserve the documented API contracts:
POST /api/v1/shorten returns 201; GET /{code} returns 302 or 404; and
GET /api/v1/links/{code}/analytics returns the code and clicks_total.
Accept absolute HTTP(S) destination URLs only.

Return a structured draft with a summary, functional and quality requirements,
assumptions, open questions, risks, ordered tasks with dependencies, tests, and
acceptance checks. Treat Q-6 and Q-7 as targets requiring measurement; do not
claim they pass without benchmark evidence. Mark the result as pending human
review. Do not treat the draft as approved implementation or external sign-off.
summary: Plan the baseline URL-shortener service from the approved assignment documents.
functional_requirements: Create short links from valid absolute HTTP(S) destination URLs.
Redirect known codes and return 404 only after confirming an unknown code.
Record click events asynchronously and expose aggregate link analytics.
quality_requirements: Use Python 3.11+, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy 2.x, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
Keep click processing idempotent and disclose the best-effort publication window.
Measure Q-6/Q-7; do not claim performance acceptance without benchmark evidence.
assumptions: The existing engineering design is the stack and API contract source for this scenario.
Custom aliases, expiration, authentication, and collection of IP/user-agent data are out of baseline scope.
open_questions: Are additional URL-validation, authentication, rate-limiting, or abuse controls required before deployment?
What representative environment and separate load generator will be used for formal Q-6/Q-7 acceptance?
risks: Local benchmark results do not establish deployed capacity or satisfy Q-6/Q-7.
A process failure before background event publication can lose a click.
